header.sector: Power generation, grid and interconnection for AI datacenters
header.title: Rate rise and datacenter moratoriums have pressured utilities exposed to the AI trade

s01_bottom_line.text: S&P 500 Utilities swung from a July peak above 10% to around -10% price return since May as datacenter moratoriums (New York, then Texas in early August) and rising Treasury yields weighed on the sector. ⟨cited figures: approximate, read from a chart; data as of 2026-09-30⟩

The article presents utilities as a microcosm of forces driving markets — the promise of AI, political consequences of the investment boom, and higher rates — rather than making an explicit buy/sell call.

The article treats utilities as both an AI enabler and a victim of political backlash and higher rates; the net effect on the sector has been sharply negative, though the article does not quantify an earnings impact, only price and P/E declines.

items.text: S&P 500 Utilities peaked above 10% in July then fell to around -10% by end of September (price return since May). ⟨cited figures: approximate, read from a chart; data as of 2026-09-30⟩
S&P 500 Utilities price and P/E peaked before the New York datacenter moratorium, then declined, with a sharper drop after Texas datacenter restrictions in early August.
State governments have placed moratoriums on datacenter build-out, weighing on the utilities sector.
Higher Treasury yields compete with utilities' dividends, weighing on the sector.
Utilities providers are key enablers of the AI datacenter build-out due to its large electricity requirements.

s03_transmission.text: AI datacenter build-out requires large electricity supply, making utilities key enablers of AI.
Rising reliance on utilities raised electricity prices for consumers, triggering political backlash and state moratoriums on build-out.

Moratoriums curtail the build-out that would drive utilities' volume growth, and higher Treasury yields erode the relative appeal of utilities' dividends; the article shows resulting price and P/E declines but does not quantify earnings.

S&P 500 Utilities fell from above 10% to around -10% price return since May, with P/E compressing after the moratorium announcements. ⟨cited figures: approximate, read from a chart; data as of 2026-09-30⟩
